summary: Same result in the working tree, different history, different consequences.

steps.say: Both stories start the same way. You branched off B, someone else pushed D to main.
Merge makes a new commit with two parents. Your C is untouched — it keeps its hash, its author date, everything.
Rebase does something different. It takes the change C introduced and replays it on top of D.
C' is not C. Same diff, new parent, new hash — a different commit wearing the same message. The original C is still in the reflog, unreferenced, until it gets collected.
steps.aside: Rebase does not move commits. It copies them.

steps.say: Which is why the rule is about audience, not aesthetics: rebase your own unpushed work freely, because nobody else has those hashes. Rebase a shared branch and everyone else's history now disagrees with yours.
